cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: As a sole proprietary business expands and needs more capital and people, which form of organisation do people usually adopt?
cards.back: As the business expands, one needs more capital and larger number of people to manage the business and share its risks. In such a situation, people usually adopt the partnership form of organisation.
cards.quote: As the business expands, one needs more capital and larger number of people to manage the business and share its risks. In such a situation, people usually adopt the partnership form of organisation.
reasons: review:Not important: introductory narrative filler with no testable point; the answer 'partnership' is given away by the chapter title.

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: New partner does not bring goodwill in cash: which accounts are debited and credited?
cards.back: Goodwill not brought by the new partner will be debited to current account of new partner while sacrificing partners' capital accounts will be credited for their respective shares.
cards.quote: Goodwill not brought by the new partner will be debited to current account of new partner while sacrificing partners' capital accounts will be credited for their respective shares.

source.section: When the new partner does not bring goodwill

reasons: review:Redundant: same answer as fact-no-goodwill-books-credit-debit and fact-part-brought-current-debited; fronts hard to tell apart.

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Name two cases in which a company can issue shares at a discount.
cards.back:
Reissue of forfeited shares; issue of sweat equity shares
As a general rule, a company cannot ordinarily issue shares at a discount. It can do so only in cases such as ‘reissue of forfeited shares’ (to be discussed later) and issue of sweat equity shares.
cards.quote: As a general rule, a company cannot ordinarily issue shares at a discount. It can do so only in cases such as ‘reissue of forfeited shares’ (to be discussed later) and issue of sweat equity shares.

source.book: Accountancy Part 2: Company Accounts and Analysis of Financial Statements
source.section: 1.6.6 Issue of Shares at a Discount

reasons: review:NCERT's own leac201 summary says only sweat equity shares can be issued at a discount (Companies Act 2013), so 'two cases' is not the single NCERT answer.

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: The amount received as premium is credited to ‘____’ whereas amount of discount allowed is debited to “____” and is written-off over the years
cards.back: The amount received as premium is credited to ‘securities premium account’ whereas amount of discount allowed is debited to “loss/discount on issue” and is written-off over the years
cards.quote: The amount received as premium is credited to ‘securities premium account’ whereas amount of discount allowed is debited to “loss/discount on issue” and is written-off over the years

source.book: Accountancy : Company Accounts and Analysis of Financial Statements

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: What can an economist judge, and what do governmental actions rest on, through analysis of the financial statements of various firms?
cards.back: Through the analysis of financial statements of various firms, an economist can judge the extent of concentration of economic power and pitfalls in the financial policies pursued. The analysis also provides the basis for many governmental actions relating to licensing, controls, fixing of prices, ceiling on profits, dividend freeze, tax subsidy and other concessions to the corporate sector.
cards.quote: Through the analysis of financial statements of various firms, an economist can judge the extent of concentration of economic power and pitfalls in the financial policies pursued. The analysis also provides the basis for many governmental actions relating to licensing, controls, fixing of prices, ceiling on profits, dividend freeze, tax subsidy and other concessions to the corporate sector.

source.book: Accountancy : Company Accounts and Analysis of Financial Statements
source.section: 4.3 Objectives of Analysis of Financial Statements

reasons: review:Not important: a long list of government actions is low-yield trivia, not a headed list or definition. Front is two-part with a multi-item answer, so no single right answer.

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Formula: Shareholders' Funds (Equity), as the sum of share capital and reserve items
cards.back: Shareholders’ Funds (Equity) = Share capital + Reserves and Surplus + Money received against share warrants + Share application money pending allotment
cards.quote: Shareholders’ Funds (Equity) = Share capital + Reserves and Surplus + Money received against share warrants + Share application money pending allotment

source.book: Accountancy: Company Accounts and Analysis of Financial Statements

cards.back:
Net Profit/Loss before Tax and Extraordinary Items
+ Deductions already made in Statement of Profit and Loss on account of xxx Non-cash items such as Depreciation, Goodwill to be Written-off.

cards.subject: accountancy
cards.front: Indirect method proforma: from Operating Profit before Working Capital changes to Net Cash from Operating Activities, in order.
cards.back:
Operating Profit before Working Capital changes
Add : in case of increase in current assets (other than cash and cash xxx equivalent) and decrease in current liabilities.
Less : in case of decrease in current assets (other than cash and cash xxx equivalent) and decrease in current liabilities.
Cash Flows from Operation Activities before Tax and Extraordinary items
– Income Tax Paid
+/– Effects of Extraordinary Items
Net Cash from Operating Activities
cards.quote: Operating Profit before Working Capital changes Add : in case of increase in current assets (other than cash and cash xxx equivalent) and decrease in current liabilities. Less : in case of decrease in current assets (other than cash and cash xxx equivalent) and decrease in current liabilities.
